--starci-core-verdict-edge.selector: /* * THE VERDICT EDGE IS SHIPPED. * * A row in a verdict collection reports an outcome, and the outcome is drawn as a 2px edge on * the row's leading side. The collection already squares its corners for exactly these rows; * this is the paint the squaring was preparing for, and without it an application had to reach * across the Grammar boundary with its own inset shadow to get it. * * It is an INSET SHADOW, not a border and not a padded rule, because the rows of a verdict * collection are usually the consumer's own children: a border would move their content two * pixels and a padding would fight the inset they already own, while a shadow paints inside the * box that is already there. The row is addressed by `data-verdict`, which is the slot contract * `SurfaceListCard` documents for its collection, so a Grammar row and an application row draw * the same edge from the same attribute. * * The offset is physical because `box-shadow` has no logical form; under `dir="rtl"` the edge * stays on the left. No shipped object mirrors yet, so this is consistent rather than a new gap. */ .starci-core-owned-collection[data-grammar-collection="verdict"] [data-verdict="success"], .starci-core-static-row[data-verdict="success"]

--starci-core-band-offset.selector: /* * THE BAND PUBLISHES ITS OWN HEIGHT. * * A page under a sticky band needs exactly one number - where the band stops - to pin a rail * beneath it, and until now every consumer RESTATED that number: `calc(4rem + 1px)` for the * primary row and its separator, `calc(4rem + 2rem + 1px)` once a feature layer is stacked. * Restated geometry is wrong the moment the band changes, so the band publishes it instead. * * It is published with `:has()` on the Grammar root, not measured in JS, because presence and * stacking are already spelled by the data attributes these compositions emit, and a custom * property set on the root inherits to every page inside it. The root - not `:root` - keeps the * package inside its own boundary, which is the same reason no rule here touches the document. * * NOTHING is defined when no sticky band is present, so `var(--starci-core-band-offset, X)` * still resolves to a consumer's own X exactly as it did before this property existed. */ .grammar-common-root:has(.starci-core-navigation-feature-nav[data-grammar-navigation-feature-nav-position="sticky"]), .grammar-common-root:has(.starci-core-subnav[data-grammar-subnav-position="sticky"])

--starci-core-band-subnav-height.selector: /* A sticky Subnav stacks under the band, so it adds its own height and separator to the offset. */ .grammar-common-root:has(.starci-core-subnav[data-grammar-subnav-position="sticky"])

/* A compact Subnav is not on screen here, so it contributes no height to the band offset. */ .grammar-common-root:has(.starci-core-subnav[data-grammar-subnav-position="sticky"][data-grammar-subnav-visibility="compact"])

--starci-core-workspace-navigation-track.selector: /* * THE COLLAPSED FORM IS THE DEFAULT here too, for the reason recorded on * `.starci-core-primary-rail-layout`: every multi-track form lives INSIDE a container query, so * the stacked one cannot be outranked by an attribute selector written outside it. Before this, * the two-track rule for `[navigation="present"][rail="present"]` (0,3,0) in the 72rem query * beat the collapse group's bare class (0,1,0), and the leading four-track rule (0,4,0) beat * every collapse rule there is, so a shell carrying a navigation and a rail never stacked. * * The tiers are mutually exclusive ranges, narrowest first: * default one column, one row per region * > 56rem the regions take their own tracks * > 72rem a navigation AND a rail stand beside the primary at the same time */ .starci-core-workspace-shell-layout

--starci-core-workspace-rail-track.selector: /* * THE COLLAPSED FORM IS THE DEFAULT here too, for the reason recorded on * `.starci-core-primary-rail-layout`: every multi-track form lives INSIDE a container query, so * the stacked one cannot be outranked by an attribute selector written outside it. Before this, * the two-track rule for `[navigation="present"][rail="present"]` (0,3,0) in the 72rem query * beat the collapse group's bare class (0,1,0), and the leading four-track rule (0,4,0) beat * every collapse rule there is, so a shell carrying a navigation and a rail never stacked. * * The tiers are mutually exclusive ranges, narrowest first: * default one column, one row per region * > 56rem the regions take their own tracks * > 72rem a navigation AND a rail stand beside the primary at the same time */ .starci-core-workspace-shell-layout
